profile.reading:
This point is mapped as NTT's VA9 building at 44710 Gigabit Plaza in Ashburn, Virginia, on the same Gigabit Plaza street as NTT's confirmed VA3, VA6, VA7, and VA8 buildings nearby. NTT's own Ashburn campus overview page names and links only seven buildings today, VA1, VA2, VA3, VA4, VA5, VA7, and VA11. VA9 does not appear anywhere in that list or elsewhere on NTT's public site, even though the street address for this entry comes from public geocoded property records placing a real structure at this location. Because NTT has not published a dedicated facility page for VA9, this entry does not assert a square footage or a megawatt figure for the building specifically, since none exists in NTT's own public materials to confirm.

NTT describes its overall Ashburn campus, as a whole, as delivering 224 megawatts of critical IT load across 78 acres in Loudoun County's Data Center Alley. That combined figure necessarily includes whatever capacity VA9 itself contributes, but NTT does not break the total out building by building for every address on the campus, so this entry cannot state VA9's individual share of that 224 megawatt figure. NTT's own numbering on this campus runs at least through VA11, the highest building number NTT names on its own site, though gaps in that sequence, including VA6, VA8, and VA9, currently have no individually published facility page despite carrying real, numbered addresses on the same streets NTT does document.

NTT's individually documented buildings on this campus offer a rough scale reference for what a typical building here looks like, though not a confirmed match for VA9. VA1, a short distance away at 44664 Guilford Drive, is confirmed on NTT's own site at 64,723 square feet of raised floor and 12.6 megawatts of critical IT load. This entry does not apply VA1's specific numbers to VA9, since NTT has never confirmed the two buildings are comparable in size or design, and building footprints visibly vary across this campus.

Virginia's data center growth is also reshaping statewide electricity rates in ways that reach every building on this campus. In November 2026, the Virginia State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates that raise a typical residential bill by about 16 dollars a month, to roughly 165 dollars, while creating a new GS-5 rate class specifically for data centers, effective January 1, 2027. Large demand campus buildings like this one face 14 year mandatory minimum contracts and cost coverage requirements under that new class, according to Inside Climate News's reporting on the commission's decision. That regulatory shift applies to the campus and to VA9's undocumented capacity alike, even though this entry cannot say how large a share of the 224 megawatt campus total VA9 itself represents.

sources.title: Virginia regulators approve new Dominion Energy rates, data center rate class

reading.body:
NTT Ashburn VA9 sits on Gigabit Plaza in the operator's sprawling Ashburn campus, which holds 224 megawatts of critical IT load across 78 acres. The facility itself does not have a published specification page, does not appear in NTT's own campus index, and carries no disclosed capacity figure. The address is geocoded to a real structure on the same cluster as four other confirmed NTT buildings, all on the same street, but NTT has not made VA9's specifications public.

The broader Ashburn campus ranks 24th among Virginia's 330 mapped data center facilities, though only 23 facilities statewide publish power figures at all. That published campus total of 224 MW must include VA9 along with named buildings like VA1 (12.6 MW at 64,723 square feet), but NTT has not broken the total down building-by-building, so VA9's share is not disclosed. If this facility matches the density of VA1, a few blocks away, it would hold roughly 12 to 13 MW, but this registry does not apply that ratio without operator confirmation.

As of January 2027, Virginia's State Corporation Commission imposed a new GS-5 rate class for large data center campuses, requiring 14-year mandatory contracts and minimum cost-coverage terms under Dominion Energy's approved rate structure. Any data center at this Ashburn location now operates under those regulatory constraints, which will materially affect the economics of hosting AI workloads in this geography. The absence of a published figure for VA9 means this particular building's role in AI scaling cannot be quantified from operator disclosure alone.
